reviews.text: My current little obsession.... Tiny Auto Knights; is a cute and endlessly fun auto battler crafted with love from a small dev team. You build your deck of Thirty heros from a growing rooster of Sixty Heros, across Five different rarities. Then you go into battle. At the start you choose from three possible heros to place on your field which can be utilized in full or re-rolled for a new selection. You start with selections of lowest tier from your deck and build upon it between battles evolving or swapping out each Hero to get the setup you desire. Each run is different as the Hero's offered to you in the shop are from a growing pool randomly drawn from your crafted deck. After exhausting your currency you send your team into battle. Battles are automatic, you watch as your team goes against other players previous runs. Win or lose you go back to the shop to continue to improve or adjust your team with the available offers. Adding on relics/items that change how your shop time plays out. From generating gold to increasing chances of higher tier Hero to making effects trigger more often (and more..). Each loss removes one health from your five possible losses for the run. Win ten battles and emerge victorious. Winning gives xp to levels you up which provides you with keys to unlock more Heros to assist with crafting your perfect deck. The light colorful art, music and sound, provide for a relaxed experience that keeps you going for one more run.. Go for the 100 poison stack I promise its hard!

[h2] 游戏介绍 [/h2] 《自走骑士团》是Mumpitz Games制作并发行的一款像素风肉鸽玩法的自走棋竞技游戏，玩家将在独特的3x3的微型棋盘上招募独特技能的骑士，在继承了传统自走棋的玩法的同时，运用策略布局并升级骑士，打造独一无二的阵容，让玩家每次战斗都能获得独特的游戏体验。 [h2] 玩法介绍 [/h2] 为了满足不同玩家的需求，制作组提供了两种模式供玩家选择，适合新手休闲玩家的休闲模式，以及自走棋老手喜欢挑战的玩家排位模式。和传统的自走棋游戏不同的是本作的商店不是公共的。开局系统会自动赠送10个金币，玩家可以购买棋子，格子，或者刷新商店买想要的棋子，随着格子增多拿到高级棋子的概率也会变大。但需要注意的是本作没有公共卡池，虽然不用担心合卡但这个比较看运气。玩家需要在一局当中总共获得十场战斗的胜利，每场游戏一共有五条命，另外不管输赢，每回合都会固定获得10枚金币。尽管有些棋子可以额外获取金币，但需要注意的是金币必须花完，无论剩多少都不能累加到下一局。 游戏的对局与传统自走棋大地图不同，放置在了一个3x3紧凑的棋盘上，虽然看似玩法比较简单，但是游戏的难度不低，在狭小的空间里。玩家需要根据不同英雄的技能合理布局，也就是说需要考虑到敌人的攻击方式，然后不断调整位置，避免被敌人追着打。为了让英雄更强还要不断合成，英雄升级比较简单，三个一级英雄就能合成二级，六个一级英雄就会合成三级。升级后不仅基础属性加强，还会有额外的可选择加成效果。游戏的战斗是全自动的，前排顶部的英雄会优先进行攻击，因此布局阶段的位置选择将直接影响战斗中的攻击顺序与技能释放时机。 另外本作支持线上对局，但是采用的是离线PVP，也就是说玩家在游戏里遇到的都是真实玩家的存档阵容搭配，系统会根据你的胜利场次和血量匹配同等条件的对手。这样的设计可以让玩家不至于随时在电脑前待命，更方便玩家随时随地开一局游戏体验。 [h2] 总结 [/h2] 虽然是一款像素风游戏，但是本作的战场细节做的很棒，游戏的机制和玩法在传统自走棋基础上做了创新，让本作的策略深度得到了加强，推荐给喜欢自走棋的玩家或者是对于肉鸽构筑有一定基础的玩家入手。 [quote]漫话漫谈，期待关注:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44551694/]写生漫话家[/url] ←节约宝贵时间，阅读省流测评~ 欢迎加入漫话家的大家庭:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/14030826]写生漫话家[/url]←共同探讨游戏中的精彩片段，向玩家展现第九艺术的魅力~

Fun auto battler, reminds me a lot of Super Auto Pets but with some cool new twists. Also quite some content with different game modes and unlockable heroes. Perfect game to play while watching a stream or listening to a podcast!
很有意思的独立游戏，用金币购买角色和刷新buff，相同角色可以2合1升级获得升级效果，到达一定程度还可以解锁自定义牌组
非常上头的自走棋游戏，套路和组合非常多~和之前的一些对战自走棋游戏差不多，对手应该是玩家镜像，但某些玩家可能是内测玩家，组合出的阵容太强大了，打不过，根本打不过！
9v9的策略肉鸽自走棋，当前版本冰冻比较强，冻了之后会被暴揍，最好多堆一点净化层数，然后下毒+死亡流也还不错，大爹养一个就够用了，目前流派还是少了点，希望后续能多一点吧
像素风肉鸽的自走棋游戏，最开始关注是觉得画风可爱，所以试了试，之前接触自走棋类型的游戏不多，不过感觉还挺好玩到底，上头上头嘿嘿，画风可爱！！
没有中评，所以差评 作为资深的自走棋爱好者，满分十分，这个最多6分 构筑少，流派少，像素又难看，20块以内可以入
网络问题很严重，教程关卡就开始了，中途只要有一次连不上服务器就没法对局，一直Check internet connection卡在那。卡网络的时间要比玩游戏的时间还长好多，50分钟新手关都还没过

If you enjoy auto-battlers such as Super Auto Pets, it's lots of fun. I played more than 11 hours in the first day of buying it. There are a few things where it's not clear if some interactions are bugged or they are intentional, but I guess I'll have to ask the devs on Discord about those interactions

5/10 Sprites, battles and music is cute! Gameplay is super repetitive, a mindless grind! When you run out of hearts you start the game all over again. The auto-battler takes your mind off things for a while but you have to be really tactical with positioning of your heroes, can be frustrating for newcomers to this genre. Game brings back memories of backback battles, which was another disaster. Devs should add the tag that this auto-battler is also rogue-lite/like. Got bored after a couple of runs and more than an hour. Almost $10 for a discounted price tag is a little too steep for this. Gonna uninstall! Update: The matchmaking system is screwed. The first few matches are alright until you hit a certain point and it's downhill from there (believe me you'll know it). I'm literally battling whales who are just one level above me with all sorts of mad buffs and insanely strong units. DON'T RECOMMEND!

随着时间的碎片化，玩家能投入到游戏中的时间越来越少，而自走棋单局时间短、随机性与趣味性强的独特优势，也得以在一众独游里逐渐凸显出来。但是回看市面上的自走棋游戏，同质化却相当严重，绝大多数是像传统的云顶之弈一般的棋盘式自走棋与近年流行的背包构建类自走棋，想要玩精通一款自走棋需要对所有的棋子都有一个大致的了解，需要消耗大量的时间也增加了学习的成本，但本评测中提到的《自走骑士团》则尝试打破这面困境，在保证游戏性的前提下将一切都趋向于了简化。那么这款游戏是否值得尝试呢？本评测将详述其功与过。 对于现在卷美术卷画质的大环境，本作采用了简单舒适的像素风，棋子各具特色且风格多样，有可爱的小动物也有童话里的公主与怪兽，但共同之处是十分可爱。随着玩家等级的提升和奖杯数量的积累，也可以在主页解锁好看的背景与头像框，也有购买支持者包解锁的内容，这个按需自取即可。 回到核心的玩法，既有练习卡组的pve模式，也有和其他玩家的卡组对抗赢取奖杯的pvp模式，游戏的核心思路在于“堆叠”与“配合”，并没有固定的流派，本以为是3*3的棋盘式动物棋，但实际上格子需要购买还是有种云顶之弈的味道，什么时候解锁格子，怎么通过棋子摆放将数值叠高，都需要玩家通过观察与思考去尝试。要“堆叠”的东西十分简单，无非生命值/攻击力/debuff这三项，没有暴击之类复杂概率计算。 自走棋玩法比较核心的部分在于卡组构建，可以通过等级提升获得钥匙来解锁新的棋子，然后自定义要出战的卡组，最简化的一点是卡组虽然有四十枚棋子，但现阶段总共可以选择的棋子也就80枚左右，相当于只需要二选一编入自己想用的就好，即使是没有解锁的棋子每周也会给一个无法编辑的试用卡组去体验，美中不足的是钥匙只能通过等级提升这个途径获取，导致想要凑齐需要的棋子需要费不少功夫，如果后续能通过一些彩蛋小成就增加钥匙获取途径想必会好很多。 接着介绍对战，一般都是自己先手，然后根据每个棋子积累的效果来先后触发，根据核心思路的不同，战斗的效果也各不一样，一定程度上也需要运气来消耗更少的金币刷新需要的棋子。有些棋子的效果比较夸张，比如全队增加伤害的独眼巨人，但是由于无法升级商店只能通过结算效果来增加高稀有度棋子的刷新概率，传说棋子需要好几轮之后才能刷新，如果没有钱升级传说棋子，可以通过触发连败奖励来解锁将等级最低的棋子一键升满级，连败奖励需要连输两次以上来解锁，但由于总共只有五颗心所以没那么多机会，所以需要合理利用连败。 目前一个比较常见的思路是利用铁匠和弓箭手来叠加护盾，当然随着棋子的解锁可供选择的思路越来越多，但现阶段依旧太少，需要后续的更新来支撑游戏内容，排位赛采取奖杯加分掉血扣分简单粗暴的计算方式，理论上只要有五个奖杯就不会掉分了，但由于大家都处在一个卡组没配齐的阶段，所以上分非常困难。但是一些小彩蛋成就的设置依然会使游戏的过程充满乐趣，推荐给每一个喜欢短流程独立游戏的玩家去尝试这部作品。 [code] 点击关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/26214428] 電玩狂熱愛好者 [/url] ，以获取更多游戏评测、资讯、攻略 [/code]

《自走骑士团》披着像素 RPG 的外衣，却把用相当简单的游戏方式把自走棋和肉鸽循环的规则融合得相当有趣。游戏里我们需要组建一堆的“盟友”，经过融合和构筑让他们慢慢变强，直到成为能横推所有对手的存在。 游戏使用了最为简单甚至有点简陋的像素风画面，各个角色的等阶倒是用颜色区分得相当分明，但角色形象倒是有那么些个不大好分辨（比如鼠王和几个老鼠角色），对比起售价来说，只是这个美术水准还是略高了点点的。 《自走骑士团》里的角色众多，每个角色还都有自己的定位、属性、风格和天赋被动。刚开始我们只需要简单的使用有限的金币来招收队员，然后把同款角色进行融合升级，然后就看着他们一窝蜂的在格子里战斗就行，简单明了，没什么大的操作空间的样子。 但这样组合而成的队伍其实是没有战斗力的，想要有一定的战斗水准，还是需要认真的研究研究各个角色的“天赋被动”的，它们有的擅长破盾、有的吃到合适的词条后火力能直接翻倍、有的本来没什么存在感，结果给它堆了几件对口装备之后突然变主力！加上装备词条还有各种连锁的激发效果，这样的队伍构筑感觉会越玩越有惊喜感。 游戏的战斗就是格子自走棋，战斗节奏还是较为紧凑的，战斗过程我们没啥好操作的，但多少还能从中看出我们的角色站位是否有问题，从而在战后修整期间可以进行调整站位什么的，来调整队伍战力构筑。 整体来说，《自走骑士团》是真的相当简单的一款肉鸽自走棋游戏，简单到我们只需要选择角色、选择融合、道具加成、调整站位这几个操作就没了，还没有什么局外成长可言。但它的游戏难度又还真的挺难，毕竟我们每个关卡的敌人似乎都是其他玩家使用过的队伍阵型，在这简单又困难的过程中能干掉所有面前的队伍，也是会有满满的成就感的。如果，价格能再合适一些，就更好了！ [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url= https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]

I would've recommended the game if it wasn't so unbelievably poorly balanced. There are only two viable builds; Thorns and fire, with fire always winning... Fire is currently so ridiculously broken that the initial hits can one-shot the whole board. Kinda ruins the fun when your only options are "you just lose" or "you won without even trying". You can certainly toy around with various other fun builds with loads of interesting units. Unfortunately fun builds are not realistic options, as you'll constantly play against the meta builds and simply have no hope of winning later matches. Talking about getting punished for wanting to have fun and just trying stuff out... You need to unlock most units by leveling up, which for some bizarre reason is a REALLY DAMN SLOW process. Especially if you don't want to just mindlessly spam the meta build.
游戏中的流派很多，策略性较强，研究排列布阵还是挺有意思的～

9 slots to place your units and you can buy units and level them up. If you buy certain amount of copies, hero will level up and you get a choice of 3 rewards. There are 2 item slots at first and you can add them to any unit. Other feature is you can freeze/hold a unit or item for the next round. You need to win 10 rounds and can lose up to 3 times. [h1] Pros: [/h1] - Multiple builds to try out such as poison, thorns, and summon units. - Easy to learn game if you have played strategy or auto battler games before. [h2]Cons: [/h2] - Getting 1 level only unlocks 1 new unit only, so it can take hours to get more units because you only get 1 key after reaching level 9/10. Common and rare units should not cost the same as a legendary to unlock. 1 key should unlock 2 of the weaker units. - Feels like rock paper scissors game. A build may hard counter you and you can't do anything about it since changing your build mid run is too expensive. For example, I had a high health build, but lost to a de-buff Satyr build. - Graphics are mediocre with pixel graphics. - Ranked mode feels extremely unbalanced. At 8-10 wins, your opponents have builds that don't seem possible with crazy high health or attack. It's possible they are generated to challenge the player and make them lose at least a few rounds. - Low player base so only hardcore players are left. I played same 3-4 opponents on 2-3 different runs and most of them have stronger builds compared to what I had. [h3]Suggestions: [/h3] - Rerolls should not expire if you don't use them. There is a relic that allows you to retain rerolls, but you need to pay 2 gold. At least allow the player to keep 1 reroll per round. - XP given per run is too low. A 9 win run gets you 1 key and that makes unlocking units glacially slow. - Include a feature for players to invite a friend to try game for a week. This game is lacking in active players and this might help with matchmaking. Newer players would have other new players to play against. [b] Conclusion: [/b] An auto battler game that is not balanced in terms of opponents in later rounds and takes too much effort to unlock new units. With the low player base, you are going to face the same players that already know the game and which builds work the best. Either you high roll a synergistic build or lose. Tiny Auto Knights, developed by Mumpitz Games and published by Mumpitz Games and Gamersky Games, is a compact auto battler that distills the genre down to its essentials while still offering enough strategic depth to keep players engaged. It operates on a simple premise—assemble a team, position it on a small grid, and let battles resolve automatically—but within that structure lies a surprisingly thoughtful system built around synergy, adaptation, and efficient decision-making. The gameplay loop is immediately accessible. Players recruit units from a rotating pool, combine duplicates to strengthen them, and arrange their lineup before combat begins. Once a battle starts, control is relinquished entirely, shifting the focus away from reflexes and toward preparation. This design creates a satisfying rhythm, where each round feels like a test of how well the player has anticipated outcomes. Positioning plays a crucial role, as even small adjustments can dramatically affect how battles unfold, particularly when dealing with units that rely on specific targeting or abilities. Where the game finds its depth is in how its units interact. Each character comes with distinct abilities, and the real challenge lies in finding combinations that complement each other effectively. Some builds focus on durability and sustain, while others lean into burst damage or scaling effects over time. The system encourages experimentation, especially as upgraded units unlock stronger or more complex abilities. At its best, the game captures the appeal of discovering a powerful synergy and watching it play out, creating moments where careful planning leads to satisfying results. The pacing is well-suited to the game’s structure. Matches are relatively short, and the asynchronous nature of its competitive mode removes the pressure of real-time play. This makes it easy to engage with in short sessions, allowing players to experiment with different strategies without committing to long play periods. The lack of direct interaction during combat also contributes to a more relaxed experience, where the emphasis remains on strategy rather than execution. Visually, Tiny Auto Knights adopts a bright and simple pixel-art style that complements its accessible design. The characters are easy to distinguish, and the battlefield remains clear even during more chaotic encounters. The presentation does not aim to impress through detail or realism, but it succeeds in maintaining readability and charm, which is essential for a game built around quick decision-making and small-scale interactions. Despite its strengths, the game does face some challenges that become more noticeable over time. Balance is one of the most prominent issues, as certain unit combinations or strategies can feel significantly stronger than others. This can limit the effectiveness of experimentation, as players may find themselves gravitating toward a smaller set of reliable builds. While the game encourages creativity, the practical viability of different approaches is not always equal, which can reduce long-term variety. Progression also introduces some friction. Unlocking new units and expanding strategic options requires repeated play, and while this can provide a sense of gradual growth, it can also feel restrictive in the early stages. Players may need to invest time before they can fully explore the range of possibilities the game offers. Combined with the balance concerns, this can make some runs feel constrained by available tools rather than purely shaped by player choice. Over extended sessions, repetition can begin to set in. The core mechanics remain consistent throughout, and while they are well-designed, they do not evolve significantly. There are no major shifts in gameplay or systems that redefine the experience, which means that the game relies heavily on its core loop to maintain engagement. For some players, this consistency is a strength; for others, it may limit long-term appeal. Even with these limitations, Tiny Auto Knights succeeds in delivering a polished and enjoyable auto battler that understands its scope. It does not attempt to compete with larger, more complex titles, instead focusing on providing a streamlined experience that is easy to learn and satisfying to play. The combination of quick matches, strategic depth, and approachable mechanics makes it particularly well-suited for players looking for a lighter take on the genre. In the end, Tiny Auto Knights is a charming and thoughtfully designed game that excels in short bursts. It offers enough depth to reward strategic thinking while remaining accessible to newcomers, even if its balance issues and limited long-term progression prevent it from reaching its full potential. For players who enjoy experimenting with builds and watching strategies unfold, it provides a consistently engaging experience within its compact design. Rating: 8/10

Total crack! This game is very addictive! Here is the play loop: - The party you buy is set up in a 3x3 grid. The ones in the right column will be fighting at the front line. As one dies, the row he/she/it is in will shift to the right. - There's a "store" (more like a tavern) where potential party members will fill a holding pen at the bottom middle of the screen. If you don't like the choices in the holding pen, click the store to fill it with new choices. If you do like any in the holding pen but can't afford them, click the gate for that pen and they will wait until the next round when you can afford them. - Buffs can be found in the lower right corner. - Other mechanisms boost the store, the grid, etc. - As you find more rare potential party members you can sell the ones in your party to replace them - Winning a whole series of battles is VERY RARE. I got that achievement and it's only been 0.1% of other players who got it too - so be prepared for winning occasional battles. In this regard the game is a bit rogue-like - you have to depend heavily on RNG after you've worked out a good strategy. From battle to battle you're optimizing your party. The battles are against other player's parties, which is pretty cool, as you can see what configurations other players have used. In this way the game is almost like a tower defense (sort of - well at least in my mind). Once all this stuff made sense, I had trouble putting the game down! Very nice and very cute! It's a keeper!
